questions.q: You are driving a truck in a convoy in dense fog. The truck ahead is going slower than you would like. May you overtake it, as shown?
options: Yes, if the oncoming lane is clear for 300 m
No: members of a convoy are forbidden to overtake one another
Yes, if you warn it by flashing your main-beam headlights
Yes, if you return to the convoy in front of it immediately
questions.explain: A member of a convoy does not break its order of movement: you may not overtake other members, leave the convoy or stop on your own, except for a forced stop. The speed is set by the convoy leader or the lead vehicle. If something hinders movement, tell the leading or rear vehicle ⟦13⟧.

questions.q: A convoy of road trains stops on the shoulder at night in a snowstorm on the leader's signal. What must be switched on on your road train during this stop?
options: Hazard warning lights, position lamps and the “Road train” sign
Only the position lamps: hazard warning lights are not needed in a convoy
Only the “Road train” sign; the other lights are switched off
Main-beam headlights, so that the convoy can be seen from far away
questions.explain: When a convoy stops on the road, hazard warning lights are switched on on all vehicles ⟦14⟧. At night and in poor visibility, position lamps ⟦15⟧ and the “Road train” sign ⟦16⟧ are lit during the stop. Main beam dazzles other drivers ⟦17⟧.

questions.q: You are turning right in a tractor unit with a semi-trailer. Why can you not start the turn as early and as close to the kerb as in a passenger car?
options: The semi-trailer wheels follow a smaller arc and will cut the corner
The tractor cab turns along a smaller arc than the semi-trailer wheels
The Rules prohibit road trains from turning from the right lane
The semi-trailer always swings into the oncoming lane on a turn
questions.explain: In a turn the rear wheels of the tractor unit and semi-trailer follow a shorter arc than the cab and cut the corner. So enter the turn later and slightly wider, moving to the adjacent lane if necessary ⟦18⟧, and watch the inside of the turn in the right-hand mirror: a pedestrian or cyclist may be there.

questions.q: The maximum authorised mass of a truck is 7 t. Which licence category (subcategory) is enough to drive it?
options: Category B
Subcategory C1
Only category C
Subcategory C1E
questions.explain: Subcategory C1 covers motor cars (except buses) with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg but not more than 7500 kg. A 7 t truck falls into C1. Category C also suffices because it includes C1, but it is not required.

questions.q: You are 19 years old, obtained subcategory C1 a year ago after an ordinary driving school and have worked as a driver since. When can you obtain category C?
options: Now: one year of experience on C1 is enough for C
From age 23, with 3 years as a driver, including a year on D1
From age 25, with 5 years as a driver on any category
From age 21, with 3 years as a driver, including a year on C1
questions.explain: Category C is obtained from age 21 with at least 3 years of work as a driver, including at least 1 year on vehicles of subcategory C1. You are 19, so you need to wait. Age 23 and experience on D1 are the requirements for category D.

questions.q: You hold category C. May you drive your truck with a trailer whose maximum authorised mass is 2 t?
options: Yes: category C allows towing a trailer of any mass
Yes, if the trailer is empty and weighs less than 750 kg
No: category C allows a trailer of up to 750 kg; you need CE
No: any trailer behind a truck needs a separate category E
questions.explain: Category C allows towing a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of no more than 750 kg. The authorised mass of your trailer is 2 t, so you need category CE. What counts is the authorised, not the actual, mass of the trailer, so an empty body does not help.

questions.q: You hold a category C licence. Do you need to obtain subcategory C1 separately to drive a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 6 t?
options: No: a C licence also gives the right to C1
Yes: subcategory C1 is always taken in a separate test
No, but only if you have more than 3 years of experience
Yes, if the truck will carry people in the body
questions.explain: A category C licence confirms the right to drive vehicles of subcategory C1 as well, just as D includes D1 and CE includes C1E. No separate C1 test is needed.

questions.q: On what vehicle is the practical test for subcategory C1 taken?
options: On a truck with a maximum authorised mass of more than 3500 kg
On a passenger car, as for the category B test
On a truck with a maximum authorised mass of exactly 7500 kg
On a tractor unit with a semi-trailer of any mass
questions.explain: The practical test is taken on a vehicle of the category for which the licence is issued. For C and C1 the Examination Rules name one vehicle: a truck with a maximum authorised mass of over 3500 kg. It is taken at an automated test ground.

questions.q: Which of these exercises do the Examination Rules provide for the practical test for category C?
options: Figure of eight
Track plank
Slalom
Coupling to a semi-trailer
questions.explain: For categories C and C1 the test ground zones are the same as for B: start, stopping and moving off on a hill, pedestrian crossing, 90-degree turns, slalom, U-turn and parking, parallel reversing parking, controlled intersection, level crossing, acceleration lane, emergency stop, finish. The figure of eight and the track plank are motorcycle exercises. The exact set and order of zones is set by the layout of your test ground.

questions.q: You are driving a truck with a maximum authorised mass of 12 t outside a built-up area on a road with a central reservation (not a motorway) and pass these signs. What is the highest speed at which you may continue?
options: 90 km/h
80 km/h
70 km/h
60 km/h
questions.explain: The upper sign “90” applies to everyone, and the lower “70” with plate 7.4.1 applies to trucks, that is, to you. Your own limit on such a road is 80 km/h, but of all the restrictions the strictest is observed: 70 km/h.

questions.q: May you use your truck with a trailer that is not designed to travel in a combination with this vehicle?
options: No: this is a condition under which use is prohibited
Yes, if the coupling device fits in size
Yes, if the authorised mass of the trailer is no more than 750 kg
Yes, over a short distance, without leaving the city
questions.explain: The Basic Provisions prohibit the use of a motor vehicle with a trailer that is not designed to travel in a combination with it. That the coupling device happens to fit in size does not change this.
